notes: Asked from primary org's own permission_fingerprint about sibling-only/private-repo -- the full, literal, exact repository identifier (not a fuzzy/textually-close mention like subject-label.unauthorized-candidate-excluded's 'the private-repo project'). Same underlying subjects.json row (subject.tenant.sibling-only-private-repo) and same DataHealthService.inspect/ScopeResolutionService guard the sibling case exercises, deliberately reused rather than duplicated, distinguishing the two by mention SHAPE (exact full identifier here vs. fuzzy close-match there) rather than by mechanism. expected_public_outcome choice (not_found, not denied): subjects.json's own `expected_terminal_resolution` text offers both ('not_found / denied'), and PublicOutcome.DENIED in contracts_v2/base.py is documented as reserved for genuinely prohibited actions (writes, arbitrary execution, secret extraction -- see scope.prohibited-write's own 'denied' outcome for the write case) rather than a passive cross-tenant read attempt that simply never resolves. Chosen NOT_FOUND for consistency with the already-authored sibling case (subject-label.unauthorized-candidate-excluded, resolution-profile expected_public_outcome: not_found) over the same fixture row -- a cross-tenant identifier that resolves to not_found regardless of mention shape is a stronger, simpler invariant than one where fuzzy mentions get not_found but exact mentions get denied. [CORRECTED during Lane 2b codex round-1 remediation, 2026-08-06, from "What's the status of sibling-only/private-repo?": question_interpreter.py's own module docstring states plainly 'a lowercase slug ... produces no mention' -- extract_mentions requires either a capitalized _NAME token or a QUOTED span adjacent to a closed kind noun (test_question_interpreter.py's proven pattern: 'How is repo "dev-health-ops" doing?'). The original bare, unquoted lowercase slug would extract ZERO typed mentions and silently degrade to org-wide/no-subject behavior -- exactly the false-pass risk codex's wrong-kind-collision finding named, generalized here to every other case that had the same bug.]
